review_candidates.title: Junior Ground Segment Software Engineer
review_candidates.description: We are looking for a software engineer at the start of their career who wants to build the systems through which satellites are planned, commanded and monitored. The role You join the team that builds our ground segment: the software through which our satellites are planned, commanded, monitored and maintained. You start on well-defined components under the guidance of a senior engineer and take on more as you learn the domain. The work is Python on the back end, React or Vue on the front end, running on Linux and in containers. The domain is space, but the craft is software. We do not expect you to arrive knowing spacecraft operations. We expect you to write clean, tested, maintainable code and to learn the domain from the people around you. You work under the ground software architect, alongside our senior ground software engineers, our ICT and DevSecOps engineer, and our security officer. What you will do Build and test features in the ground segment software: mission planning, monitoring and control, and the interfaces to the ground stations and to the customer’s systems. Write the automated tests for what you build, and keep them running in the pipeline. Build and maintain the operator-facing front ends in React or Vue, working from what operations actually needs and not from a specification alone. Develop and debug on Linux, and package what you build to run in containers. Work on the REST APIs and the event-driven interfaces between our components and with external systems. Take part in code review, both as author and as reviewer. Investigate and fix defects found in test and in operations, and write up what you found. Keep the documentation of your components accurate as they change. What is yours, and what is not You own the components assigned to you: the code, the tests, the defects and the documentation. The architecture, the external interfaces and the release decisions sit with the ground software architect and the senior engineers. You are expected to participate in software design, ask questions and challenge areas you disagree with. What you bring Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science or equivalent. Experience with Python. Experience in frontend development using React or Vue.js. Experience writing automated tests. Experience developing and debugging software on Linux. Proficiency with Git and experience in collaborative code review workflows. Understanding of REST APIs and event-driven systems. Understanding of relational database design. Understanding of network communication protocols. Understanding of software design principles, clean code practices, and maintainable software architectures. Familiarity with containerization technologies such as Docker. Professional working proficiency in English; Dutch is an advantage. Desirable Experience with satellite ground systems, spacecraft operations, or mission control software. Knowledge of CCSDS standards or space communications protocols. Exposure to real-time, embedded, mission-critical, or safety-critical software. Familiarity with CI/CD practices and tools such as GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or Jenkins. Where you can grow Two directions, depending on where your strength turns out to be. In depth, towards senior ground software engineer, owning the heaviest components and the design decisions inside them. In breadth, towards ground segment engineering, mission operations or DevSecOps, where the software work meets the system and the operators. Which one opens up depends on what you show, not on time served. What we offer A first engineering role on the system through which a satellite is operated, with experienced engineers to learn from. Competitive, market-aligned salary and benefits, and room to grow as the organisation scales. On-site work in Delft, limited hybrid working possible. Particularities This role requires Dutch security screening. You will need a VOG (Certificate of Conduct) to start, which is quick to obtain and lets you begin work on the project immediately. You might also need a VGB-B clearance. This takes longer, and we support you through it. It is required for some aspects of the role, so you must be eligible for it and willing to undergo the screening, but you do not need to have it in hand to join us. Interested? Apply via the vacancy on LinkedIn or the registration form on our website. In your application, include a short description of one thing you have built: what it does, one decision you made in the design, and what you would do differently now. It can be from your studies, a side project or a job. Applications without this description will not be reviewed. At Axient Systems we are building sovereign Dutch defence and space capability. From Delft, at the heart of the Dutch aerospace ecosystem, we work for the Netherlands Ministry of Defence and other government and commercial customers across space systems engineering, modelling & simulation, and critical asset security. Our modelling & simulation team develops and operates platforms such as DomeinSIM, our multi-domain simulation platform, alongside Titan Forge and DomeinGARD. We apply them to integrated air and missile defence (IAMD), seabed security, space missions, and the protection of critical assets.

review_candidates.title: Senior Software Engineer
review_candidates.description: About Atlas Medical Data Group We are a founder-owned portfolio of healthcare businesses. The anchor is a healthcare price intelligence company that processes the price transparency files insurers are required to publish. These files disclose the rates they have negotiated with providers but are so massive and messy that almost no one can use them. We build the technology to turn the raw data into price intelligence, which has powerful applications across the US healthcare landscape. One of the first applications is in care delivery. The data shows us which clinics have room to negotiate better rates on their commercial contracts. We buy or partner with those clinics, help them win those rates, and run their back office through our management services organization. This year we acquired the first one, a multi-site autism therapy (ABA) practice. About the role We are hiring a senior software engineer to build and run the applications that power our growing autism therapy (ABA) platform: the practices we operate and the management services organization (MSO) that provides them with their non-clinical operations. The role sits with the operations team and works directly with the people who run the practices on real workflow problems: referrals and intake, authorizations, scheduling, billing and collections, and the reporting that runs on top of them. The platform is built to grow. We expect to bring additional ABA practices into the portfolio and to offer the MSO's services to practices outside it. The applications this person builds are meant to run across many practices, not one. Our practices provide ABA therapy to children with autism and their families. The software available to ABA practices is poor, and the cost of that lands on clinicians, who spend time on administration that should go to clients, and on families, who wait longer to get into care. Better tools change both. Why this role exists The off-the-shelf software available to ABA practices (practice management, claims, scheduling) does not serve them well. We intend to replace or supplement those systems with purpose-built tools, using AI tooling and open source where it fits, rather than keep configuring vendor software. The goal is software, built with our clinical and operations team, that is better than the commercial products ABA practices pay for today. The MSO will provide billing, credentialing, scheduling, finance, and reporting services to our practices and to others that join the portfolio. The applications and data that support those services are being built now, and the design has to anticipate more than one organization. What you will do Build applications end to end: understand the operational problem with the people who do the work, design the solution, build the data model, back end, and front end, deploy it, and support it in production. Work the practice's core workflow one capability at a time, following the client journey with priority going to the current pain points: outreach and referral management, intake and benefits verification, authorizations, clinic scheduling (a first application is already in place), session documentation through to claims, billing, payment posting, and collections, and operational reporting over each of the above. Automate manual and repetitive operational work where a purpose-built tool, a script, or an AI-enabled workflow does the job better than the current system. Build on our open-source ERP, which is the one fixed point in the platform. The practice management, claims, and scheduling software around it is poor, and much of the work is replacing it. Until a replacement is in place, you integrate with what is there. Build on the established platform: deploy following the patterns in place, write deployment scripts and small infrastructure changes when needed, and contribute to the data warehouse as applications create or consume data. Build with AI as a core part of how you work, and keep finding better ways to do it as the tools change. Build applications that make use of AI where it adds something for the operators. Run the product side of what you build. You work directly with the operators and with company leadership to draw out requirements, shape what gets built and in what order, and put working software in front of them early. The business sets the priorities; you own turning them into a product that works. Who we are looking for A senior full-stack software engineer. Comfortable across data, back end, front end, and deployment. Real depth in at least one area and working competence in the rest. Which languages and frameworks you have used matters less than how well you build. Exposure to data engineering or data warehousing is a plus. 6 or more years building and shipping software, with a record of owning and running production systems and of staying in a role long enough to grow in it and to live with the decisions made there. Has shipped applications that real users depend on and has supported them after launch. A self-starter. Faced with an unfamiliar system or problem, you dig in and work it out without being told how. Works well with ambiguity. Can take a loosely defined operational problem, ask the right questions of the people doing the work, and get to a usable first version quickly. Biases toward getting a working tool into the hands of the business and improving it from there, rather than building the complete version before anyone sees it. AI-forward. You develop with AI every day, you keep changing how you work as the tools improve, and you can show what that looks like in your own work. Communicates clearly and directly with non-technical people. You will be working with clinic operators and company leadership, not picking up tickets. Healthcare, revenue cycle, or ABA experience is helpful but not required. Experience working with healthcare data or protected health information under HIPAA is preferred. Willingness to learn the domain by sitting with the operators matters more. Comfortable working remotely with a small, distributed team and communicating clearly in writing. A public GitHub profile, open source work, or a portfolio of things you have built is a plus. Include a link if you have one. What the role offers You own what you build end to end, from the first conversation with the operators through design, build, deployment, and support. There is no hand-off to another team. You ship to real users on short cycles. The people using what you build are a few steps away, and feedback comes back the same week. You have real say in the technology. We favor open source, and the open-source ERP at the center of our platform is settled. Most of what gets built on and around it, including frameworks, tooling, and the architecture of new applications, is yours to shape. We are an AI-forward team, and how we build software keeps changing. If that is the work you want to be doing, you will have the room and the company to do it. The role grows with the business. As the portfolio adds practices and the engineering footprint grows with it, the person in this seat is positioned to lead that work. What is hard about it Small team. You will be the engineer on most of what you build, and there is no larger engineering organization behind you to lean on. Healthcare. The applications handle protected health information, and HIPAA and payer requirements constrain how things get built, deployed, and accessed. Vendor systems. The practice management, claims, and payer systems our practices use today are poor and will not go away all at once. Some of the work is living with them and integrating around them while replacements get built. Ambiguity. Requirements come from operators describing their work, not from a product team with written specs. Part of the job is doing that translation yourself. Technical environment Applications have been deployed on Azure Container Apps so far, and we expect to follow established or emerging patterns as we stand up and expand the technical capabilities and infrastructure. Data warehouse on Azure; multi-organization support still to be designed. A Python-based open-source ERP as the ERP and finance platform and a base for new applications. We prefer open source and build on it where we can. Existing clinic scheduling application as the reference pattern for build and deploy. Languages and frameworks are not fixed. Existing code is largely Python (data engineering, the scheduling app, and the ERP), and choices for new applications are at the engineer's discretion based on what is being built. AI developer tooling (Claude Code or equivalent) in daily use. Logistics Location: remote, US-based. Work authorization: you must be authorized to work in the United States. We are not able to sponsor work visas for this role. Employment type: full-time employee. This is a long-term, direct-hire role, and that is where we want to end up. If you are not in a role right now, or are otherwise free to start right away, we are glad to begin with a short paid contract. Working together is the fastest way for both sides to decide, and it shortens our process considerably.
